draft.title: Affirming and challenging values
card: Values are the beliefs and attitudes a society treats as important or right. Every text carries some, in what it praises, mocks or treats as normal.
a text supports the values of its time. It presents them as sensible or admirable, and rewards characters who hold them.
a text pushes against the values of its time. It may show them as unfair or harmful, and may give sympathy to characters who resist them.
To tell which a text does, compare the values it presents with the values common in the context it was made in. A text can also affirm some values and challenge others.
draft.remember: Compare what the text values with what its time valued. That shows whether it affirms or challenges.

a.q: Which description best fits a text that challenges the values of its time?
opts: It shows a widely held attitude as unfair and harmful
It rewards characters who follow the attitudes of its time
It avoids showing any attitudes or beliefs at all
It is set in a different time from when it was written
a.why: Challenging means pushing against the attitudes of the time, such as by showing them as unfair. Rewarding characters who follow those attitudes would affirm them instead.
a.clue: Challenging means pushing against what most people believed.

b.q: A novel written in 1890 is set in a town where most people believe girls do not need schooling. The narrator admires Ada, a girl who teaches herself to read in secret, and shows the townspeople's belief as narrow-minded. What does the novel do?
opts: Challenges the values of its time about girls and education
Affirms the values of its time about girls and education
Neither, because Ada is only one character in the story
Affirms them, because the novel is set in the past
b.why: The common belief of the time was that girls did not need schooling. The novel admires Ada and presents that belief as narrow-minded, so it challenges it. Being set in the past does not make a text affirm the values of its time.
b.clue: Compare the narrator's attitude with the attitude of the townspeople.

a.best: It shows a widely held attitude as unfair and harmful

b.best: Challenges the values of its time about girls and education

a.q: Which description best fits a text that challenges the values of its time?

Affirms the common view of girls' schooling in 1890
Neither, as only one character resists that view
